k-t-b.rootDescription: Triliteral root k-t-b relating to writing, recording, and documentation.
k-t-b.phoneticArticulation: /k/ voiceless velar stop, /t/ voiceless alveolar stop, /b/ voiced bilabial stop
k-t-b.usageNote: In Levantine, the active participle kaatib is used for ongoing actions: ana kaatib = I am writing.
k-t-b.clinicalUtility: Essential for documentation instructions. iktib il-adwiye = write down the medications.
k-t-b.sentenceEnglish: The doctor is writing the report.
k-t-b.mnemonic: KiTaB (book) comes from K-T-B. Books are written.

d-r-s.rootDescription: Triliteral root d-r-s relating to study, learning, and education.
d-r-s.phoneticArticulation: /d/ voiced alveolar stop, /r/ alveolar trill, /s/ voiceless alveolar fricative
d-r-s.etymology: Proto-Semitic *drs. Related to Hebrew דרש (darash) meaning to seek/inquire.
d-r-s.usageNote: Madrasa (school) derives from this root - the place where d-r-s happens.
d-r-s.clinicalUtility: Useful for patient education. laazim tidrus 3an mara9ak = you need to learn about your condition.
d-r-s.mnemonic: DaRS = lesson. MaDRaSa = school. Study happens at school.
